title: Biological molecular asymmetry may originate from circularly polarised sunlight

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Biological molecular asymmetry may originate from circularly polarised sunlight

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The one-handed molecular asymmetry of organic products need not be a prerogative of life; it may have started from a non-vital asymmetric force, such as sunlight circularly polarised by reflection from the sea, which acts unequally on right- and left-handed molecules.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: an example limited but yet crucial (_if confirmed_), of an asymmetric force, non-vital in its origin, which might conceivably be the starting-point of that asymmetry which is characteristic of so many organic products.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Molecular asymmetry and its origin”. Scope: optically active (chiral) compounds produced by living organisms; origin of biological homochirality

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-03: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.29

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The physical submechanism is testable, but the historical-origin claim requires substantial assumptions about unavailable initial conditions. Existing data could constrain plausibility but cannot resolve whether this process started biological homochirality.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Combine measurements of marine circularly polarized sunlight with wavelength-specific asymmetric photolysis data for plausible prebiotic chiral compounds, then model whether the observed sign and magnitude could generate biological homochirality. Refutation would require showing the mechanism is absent or quantitatively insufficient under plausible early-Earth conditions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Present-day optical and laboratory data cannot identify a unique historical cause.

Early-Earth illumination and substrates are unobserved.

Many competing symmetry-breaking mechanisms make outcomes weakly discriminating.

fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.15
discriminating power: 0.25
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data existence: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Only the physical adequacy of a non-living polarizing force is measurable with existing photochemistry and atmospheric optics, and those results sit in papers rather than in one open dataset. Nothing public records the polarization and chemistry of the prebiotic sea surface at the origin of homochirality. The hypothesis is therefore only weakly separable from other asymmetric forces, and only the proxy, not the origin, can be examined now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test two proxies: whether sunlight reflected from the sea is sufficiently circularly polarized, and whether that polarization produces a measurable enantiomeric excess in relevant molecules. Either failure weakens the proposed starting force; success still leaves rival origins of biological homochirality standing.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Parity violation, chance amplification and other chiral biases predict the same biological handedness.

The wording is that asymmetry may have started this way, so a successful laboratory effect does not identify the historical cause.
